label: Cover
notes: One line: Steward runs the estate the factory stands on — Mason ships artifacts and stops at the registry, Doctor observes and prescribes, Steward deploys, provisions, and operates. Adopted 2026-07-23 when the ownership audit found Deployment and Operations orphaned between stations.

label: Act I — The Provisioner
notes: Act I: the orphaned stage. The Implementation view names Deployment and Operations as a first-class SDLC stage — in the crew it fell between two chairs until the Steward sat down.

label: Privilege drift
notes: Mindset one: no privilege outlives its deployment. The live case on the desk: the JFROG API key that attaches to every outbound request regardless of host — Doctor finds it, Steward remediates it and owns the key lifecycle from then on.

label: Budgets are governance
notes: Mindset two: the Taxonomy view's resource governance made real — machine-readable ceilings, like locking infrastructure at 1500 dollars a month, enforced with alerts, not hoped about in a wiki.

label: Act II — The duties
notes: Act II: the four duties and the CLI they will grow.

label: The four duties
notes: The duties and the CLI: provision runners and environments before Doctor's pre-flight ever runs; deploy services, not just artifacts; audit, rotate, and revoke keys; enforce resource ceilings. Incident response rides on all four.

label: Act III — Already steward-shaped
notes: Act III: the duties are already being done — by hand, without a name.

label: The estate today
notes: Three working proofs: the Pages program console deploys — today a hand-run dashboard-gen plus push; the pixi environment estate with its environment.yaml sync discipline; and the air-gap routing machinery awaiting an operator. All Steward duties, done manually.

label: Deploy services, not artifacts
notes: The differentiator versus Mason: Mason's job ends when the artifact reaches the registry. The Steward's job starts there — the service on the platform, hardened, budgeted, keyed, observed, and answered-for when it breaks.

label: Keep the lights on
notes: Close on the motto: nothing the factory needs is missing, and nothing it no longer needs stays privileged. Provision the line, hold the keys, keep the lights on.
